authoredSolutions.6: At \(t=0\) the inductor is an open circuit, so the left branch (\(5\Omega + 1\Omega = 6\Omega\)) and right branch (\(5\Omega + 4\Omega = 9\Omega\)) are simply in parallel across \(E\): \(i = \frac{E}{6} + \frac{E}{9} = \frac{5E}{18}\). At \(t=\infty\) the inductor is a short, joining the outer nodes, so the top arms (\(5\Omega \| 5\Omega = 2.5\Omega\)) are in series with the bottom arms (\(1\Omega \| 4\Omega = 0.8\Omega\)), giving \(R = 3.3\Omega\) and \(i = \frac{E}{3.3} = \frac{10E}{33}\). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.32: \(H_2O_2\) acts as an oxidising agent when it oxidises another species, its oxygen going from \(-1\) to \(-2\). In \(2I^- + H_2O_2 + 2H^+ \rightarrow I_2 + 2H_2O\), iodide is oxidised to iodine, so here \(H_2O_2\) is the oxidant. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.37: The major product of this reaction is propanal, \(CH_3CH_2CHO\). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.45: \(CrO_3\)-\(H_2SO_4\) (Jones reagent) is a strong oxidant that takes ethanol past the aldehyde stage all the way to acetic acid, so it does not yield acetaldehyde. The other routes stop at acetaldehyde, so the reaction that fails is option (A).
authoredSolutions.46: p-Aminoazobenzene forms by coupling a benzenediazonium salt with aniline, which requires the nitro group reduced to an amine and then diazotised with \(HNO_2\). Reactions (A) and (C) do this (Sn/HCl reduction, then \(HNO_2\), then coupling); reaction (B) uses \(NaBH_4/NaOH\), which neither reduces the aromatic nitro group to an amine nor forms a diazonium salt, so only (B) fails. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.48: HCl adds across the ring double bond by Markovnikov's rule to give the alkyl chloride A. \(NaI\) in dry acetone (Finkelstein reaction) then exchanges chloride for iodide, giving the alkyl iodide B. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.61: For real and equal roots, \(b^2 = 4ac\) with \(a,b,c \in \{1,\dots,6\}\): \(b=2\ (ac=1)\), \(b=4\ (ac=4: (1,4),(2,2),(4,1))\), \(b=6\ (ac=9: (3,3))\) — 5 favourable triples out of \(6^3 = 216\). Hence the probability is \(\frac{5}{216}\), option (D).
authoredSolutions.62: From \(l+m-n=0\), \(n=l+m\); substituting into \(l^2+m^2-n^2=0\) gives \(l^2+m^2=(l+m)^2\), so \(lm=0\). One line then has \(l=0\), i.e. \((0,\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2},\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2})\), and the other \(m=0\), i.e. \((\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2},0,\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2})\), so \(\cos\alpha=\tfrac12\). Then \(\cos^2\alpha=\tfrac14,\ \sin^2\alpha=\tfrac34\), giving \(\sin^4\alpha+\cos^4\alpha=\tfrac{9}{16}+\tfrac{1}{16}=\tfrac{5}{8}\). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.63: Using \(1-\cos2\theta = 2\sin^2\theta\) and \(\sin2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\), the integrand simplifies to \(\cos\theta\,(\sin^6\theta+\sin^4\theta+\sin^2\theta)\sqrt{2\sin^4\theta+3\sin^2\theta+6}\). The substitution \(t=\sin\theta\) then reduces it to a standard integral whose value is the expression in option (C).
authoredSolutions.69: The line \(2x+y=1\) has slope \(-2\), so the perpendicular tangent has slope \(\tfrac12\). A tangent to \(y^2=6x\) of slope \(m\) is \(y=mx+\tfrac{3/2}{m}\); with \(m=\tfrac12\) this is \(y=\tfrac{x}{2}+3\), i.e. \(x-2y+6=0\). Testing the points, \((5,4)\) gives \(5-8+6=3\neq0\), so it does NOT lie on the tangent. Hence option (D).
